title: Propagation and Stock Preparation of Temperate Bacteriophage ΦV10::NanoLuc in Escherichia coli
author: Caleb L Waddell
materials: Count plaques and calculate phage titer in PFU/mL.

steps.title: Prepare E. coli O157:H7C7927 Starter Culture
steps.instruction: Inoculate 100 mL LB (10 g tryptone, 10 g NaCl, 5 g yeast extract per L) in a 250–500 mL Erlenmeyer flask with 100 µL of a frozen or working culture of E. coli O157:H7C7927.

substeps.instruction: Incubate overnight at 37 °C with shaking at 100 rpm.

steps.title: Enrich for ΦV10::NanoLuc-infected Cells
steps.instruction: Infect the host culture and select for lysogens using kanamycin.

substeps.instruction: Add 100 µL of the overnight C7927 culture and 100 µL of ΦV10::NanoLuc stock phage to a fresh 100 mL LB flask.
Incubate at 37 °C and 100 rpm for 1 hour 30 minutes.
Add 100 µL of 50 mg/mL kanamycin stock (final concentration 50 µg/mL).
Continue incubation at 37 °C and 100 rpm overnight.

steps.title: Isolate ΦV10::NanoLuc Lysogens
steps.instruction: Streak the enriched culture to isolate single colonies.

substeps.instruction: Streak a loopful of the kanamycin-selected culture onto LB agar plates containing 1.4% (w/v) agar and 50 µg/mL Kanamycin.
Incubate plates overnight at 37 °C.
Select a single, well-isolated colony (presumed E. coli O157:H7C7927[ΦV10::NanoLuc] lysogen).

steps.title: Induce Prophage Production
steps.instruction: Grow the lysogen and induce phage release using mitomycin C.

substeps.instruction: Inoculate a sterile 1 L storage flask containing 2×YT broth (no antibiotic) with the selected colony.
Incubate at 37 °C and 100 rpm until the culture reaches an OD600 of 0.2–0.3.
Add mitomycin C to a final concentration of 1 µg/mL.
Continue incubation at 37 °C and 100 rpm for up to 24 h.

steps.title: Harvest Crude Lysate
steps.instruction: Collect the phage-containing supernatant from the induced culture.

substeps.instruction: Distribute the culture into 300 mL HDPE centrifuge bottles.
Centrifuge at 8,000 × g for 15 min at 4 °C to pellet bacteria and debris.
Carefully decant or pipette the supernatant (crude lysate) into a clean bottle, avoiding the pellet.

steps.title: Clarify Lysate with Chloroform
steps.instruction: Use chloroform to separate phases and eliminate remaining bacteria.

substeps.instruction: Add 10 mL chloroform per ~1 L lysate to the clarified lysate.
Gently invert several times to mix (do not shake vigorously or use a stir bar).
Incubate the mixture open/unlidded at 37 °C with mild shaking (~60 rpm).
Once phases are separated, gently pour off the upper aqueous phage-containing phase.
If necessary, use a narrow graduated cylinder and pipette to remove only the aqueous phase.

steps.title: Purify and Concentrate Phage
steps.instruction: Further clarify and concentrate the phage using centrifugation and filtration.

substeps.instruction: Pool the chloroform-treated aqueous lysate and centrifuge again at 8,000 × g for 15 min at 4 °C.
Filter the lysate through a 0.22 µm filter into a sterile 1 L glass bottle.
Add 5 M NaCl to bring the final NaCl concentration to 1M (accounting for NaCl already in the medium).

steps.title: Sucrose Cushion Centrifugation
steps.instruction: Concentrate the phage using a sucrose cushion.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 50 mL HDPE centrifuge tubes compatible with a high-speed rotor.
For each tube, either add 10 mL sterile 30% sucrose to the bottom then layer 30 mL lysate on top, or inject 10 mL 30% sucrose beneath 30 mL lysate using a needle.
Centrifuge at 48,000 × g for 1 h at 4 °C.
Pour off the supernatant and sucrose layer without disturbing the pellet.
Gently rinse each pellet with a small volume of chilled sterile deionized water.
Resuspend each pellet in ~2 mL SM phage buffer (no gelatin) and combine all resuspensions into a common 50 mL conical tube.

steps.title: Diafiltration and Final Concentration
steps.instruction: Use Amicon Ultra-15 devices to concentrate the phage and remove impurities.

substeps.instruction: Prime each Amicon Ultra-15 100 kDa device with 1 mL SM buffer and centrifuge at ~4,000 × g for ~3 min; discard flow-through.
Load up to 15 mL of the SM-resuspended phage into each device.
Centrifuge at up to 6,000 × g until the retained volume is approximately 100–200 µL (initial spin time ~8 min).
Optionally recover concentrate or add fresh SM buffer to the top chamber to return volume to 15 mL for diafiltration.
Repeat the concentration and dilution cycles (e.g., ≥4 cycles) until NanoLuc luminescence in the permeate/stock is reduced to the desired level.
Recover the final concentrated phage into a low-binding tube.

steps.title: Titer and Luminescence Measurement
steps.instruction: Determine the PFU/mL and luminescence of the phage stock.

substeps.instruction: Prepare soft agar (0.7% agar) in LB or 2×YT, optionally supplemented with 10 mM MgSO4 and 5 mM CaCl2.
Prepare a fresh overnight C7927 culture and dilute into log-phase.
Make 10-fold serial dilutions of the phage stock in SM buffer.
Mix a fixed volume of phage dilution (e.g., 100 µL) with a defined volume of log-phase C7927 (e.g., 100–200 µL).
Add the mixture to ~3–4 mL molten soft agar (45–50 °C), mix gently, and overlay onto pre-warmed bottom agar plates.
Solidify and incubate plates overnight at 37 °C.
Mix an aliquot of phage stock with NanoGlo or equivalent NanoLuc substrate per manufacturer's instructions and measure RLUs on a luminometer or plate reader.
Record titer (PFU/mL), luminescence values, and number of Amicon cycles.

steps.title: Aliquot and Store Phage Stock
steps.instruction: Store the concentrated ΦV10::NanoLuc stock in labeled cryovials.

substeps.instruction: Aliquot stock into sterile, labeled cryovials (e.g., 0.2–1 mL per aliquot).
Store short-term at 4 °C or long-term at −80 °C.
Label vials with: Phage (ΦV10::NanoLuc), Host (C7927), Date, PFU/mL, Number of Amicon cycles, Storage buffer (SM ± gelatin), and Operator initials.
